updates.name: As a Metro by T-Mobile authorized dealer, I want to knock money off an accessory before I put it on the invoice, so that I can honour a price I have promised a customer without calling a manager
updates.custom_requirements:
## What this test is about
Reps are often asked to come down on the price of an accessory - a customer buying a phone and a case together expects something off, or a manager has promised a walk-in a deal. Accessory Sale lets the rep do that at the counter, without anyone else's approval, as long as the new price stays inside a range the business sets per item: a floor the store will not sell below, and a ceiling which is the item's normal list price, since this is a discount and never a mark-up. The rep can express the same discount in whichever way the conversation went - the price they agreed, a percentage off, or a number of dollars off - and all three arrive at the same figure. The discount is measured from the item's list price, and tax is then charged on the reduced price, not the original one, so the customer is never taxed on money they did not pay. This test walks a rep applying a discount all three ways to the same taxed accessory, checking each time that the tax shrinks with the price, and then putting it on the invoice at the reduced price plus the reduced tax.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2788 (Price Adjustments for Cart Items - Quick Sale flow), RTPL-2965 (Accessory price adjustment in the Payment flow)

## Preconditions
- The rep is signed in at store EZLOGIC.
- The till has no customer tablet paired to it, so the sale goes straight from the invoice to the payment screen.
- The invoice is empty at the start.
- This accessory is taxed at this store at 10 percent of the price charged, so the Final price shown in the panel is always the price after discount plus that tax.

## Test data
- **Accessory to discount:** Item number 77-53942, OTTERBOX SYMMETRY SERIES FOR APPLE IPHONE 7 PLUS - HALFTONE 624 (WHITE WITH, list price $39.99, in stock, taxed  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-14, Browse accessories search and item detail panel: Price $39.99, Tax $4.00, Discount ($0.00), Final price $43.99)_
- **Allowed range:** $32.99 MIN, $39.99 MAX  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-14, Price adjustment section of the item detail panel)_
- **Agreed price to set:** $35.00  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-14, typed live - Discount ($4.99), Tax $3.50, Final price $38.50, accepted and added to the invoice)_
- **Percentage to take off:** 10 percent  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-14, typed live - Discount ($4.00), Tax $3.60, Final price $39.59)_
- **Dollars to take off:** $5.00  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-14, typed live - Discount ($5.00), Tax $3.50, Final price $38.49)_

## Screens (design reference)
- **Item detail with the Price adjustment panel, price set to $35.00** — screenshot: `screens/live-2026-10-14-01-tax-on-discount-77-53942.png` (attach from the run folder)
- **Invoice with the discounted line** — screenshot: `screens/live-2026-10-14-02-invoice-taxed-discount.png` (attach from the run folder)
- **Payment screen asking for the discounted price plus tax** — screenshot: `screens/live-2026-10-14-03-payment-taxed-discount.png` (attach from the run folder)

## Automation Notes
- The money check that matters most: the invoice line, Total due and the payment screen's Collect amount must all carry $38.50 - the discounted $35.00 plus $3.50 tax. $43.99 (full price plus full tax) or $39.00 ($35.00 plus the $4.00 full-price tax) would both be defects.
- The QTY figure changes whenever anyone sells or receives this item on the test environment, so check only that it is above zero - never assert an exact count.
- Check the Tax figure at every step, not just the Final price: it must move with the discount ($4.00 at list, $3.50 at $35.00, $3.60 at 10 percent off, $3.50 at $5.00 off).
- Step 6 is real behaviour, not a test glitch: switching method keeps the number in the box and re-reads it in the new method. Assert that the out-of-range result is refused there - a switch that silently let a 35 percent discount through would be a defect.
- Type into the Amount box key by key, as a person would; select the whole box before typing a new figure. Type whole figures such as 35 - the box adds the cents itself, and typing 3500 is read as $3,500.00.
- Clean up afterwards by cancelling the sale (Cart options, Cancel cart) so the next run starts with an empty invoice.
- If 77-53942 no longer shows a range ($32.99 MIN, $39.99 MAX), is no longer taxed, has sold out, or is refused as not approved when added, do not hunt for another item alone: contact the manual QA team to get an approved, taxed, in-stock accessory with a price range for this store. Items 77-55705 ($34.99 to $39.99) and 77-57163 ($69.99 to $89.99) had the same profile on 2026-10-14.

The buttons offered are Remove from invoice and Update item. Closing the panel leaves the invoice unchanged at Total due $38.50.

steps.action: Click Continue
steps.expected: The PAYMENT screen opens reading Collect $38.50 with cash, card, or split the payment across multiple methods. The invoice panel reads Inventory $38.50, Total due $38.50 and Balance due $38.50 - the customer is asked for the discounted price plus the tax on that discounted price.

steps.action: Stop here - do NOT take any payment and do NOT click Submit
steps.expected: The sale is left unpaid on the payment screen. Nothing is sold and the store's stock count is untouched.

updates.name: As a Metro by T-Mobile authorized dealer, I want to be stopped when I try to sell an accessory below the store's floor price or above its list price, so that I cannot give away margin or overcharge a customer by mistyping
updates.custom_requirements:
## What this test is about
Letting a rep set their own price at the counter is only safe if there is a fence around it. The business sets a floor per accessory - the least the store is prepared to sell it for - and the ceiling is the item's ordinary list price, because this is a discount and a rep must never be able to charge a customer more than the shelf price. There is deliberately no manager override in this version: a price outside the range is simply refused, for everyone, with a message that names the limit that was breached so the rep knows what they are allowed to do. This matters in both directions. Below the floor the store loses margin on every sale, and a mistyped figure - a missing decimal point - could hand an accessory over for almost nothing. Above the ceiling the customer is overcharged. This test types a price just outside each end of the range and checks that both are refused and that neither reaches the invoice.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2788 (Price Adjustments for Cart Items - Quick Sale flow)

## Preconditions
- The rep is signed in at store EZLOGIC.
- The till has no customer tablet paired to it.
- The invoice is empty at the start.
- This accessory is not taxed at this store: its Tax settings section shows Apply tax with Yes and No both unavailable, and Tax reads $0.00 throughout. The amounts below are therefore the discounted price with no tax added.

## Test data
- **Accessory to price:** Item number 141761-5085, IPHONE 13 PRESIDIO PERFECT-CLEAR WITH GRIP+MS (CLEAR/CLEAR), list price $100.00, in stock  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-09, Browse accessories search and item detail panel)_
- **Allowed range:** $96.00 MIN, $100.00 MAX  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-09, Price adjustment section of the item detail panel)_
- **Price below the floor:** $95.00  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-09, typed live - refused with Price below minimum value $96.00.)_
- **Price exactly on the floor:** $96.00  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-09, typed live - accepted, Final price $96.00)_
- **Price exactly on the ceiling:** $100.00  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-09, typed live - accepted, Final price $100.00)_
- **Price above the ceiling:** $101.00  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-09, typed live - refused with Price above maximum value $100.00.)_

## Screens (design reference)
- **Item detail with the Price adjustment panel** — screenshot: `screens/live-2026-10-09-01-discount-141761.png` (attach from the run folder)

## Automation Notes
- Check both halves of each refusal: the message appears AND Add accessories is greyed out. A message shown while the item can still be added at the bad price is the defect this case exists to catch.
- The QTY figure changes whenever anyone sells or receives this item on the test environment, so check only that it is above zero - never assert an exact count.
- The two exact-edge prices must be accepted. A floor or ceiling that refuses its own value is a defect too.
- Each message names the limit that was breached, so assert the amount in the text as well as the wording.
- Type into the Amount box key by key, as a person would; select the whole box before typing a new figure. Setting the value directly without key presses leaves the panel unchanged.
- There is no manager override in this version, so expect a flat refusal for every user and no approval prompt anywhere in the flow.
- If 141761-5085 no longer shows a range ($96.00 MIN, $100.00 MAX), has sold out, or is refused as not approved when added, do not hunt for another item alone: contact the manual QA team to get an approved, in-stock accessory with a price range for this store.

updates.name: As a Metro by T-Mobile authorized dealer, I want an accessory that is not on the carrier's approved list to be refused when I try to sell it, so that the store never sells a product it is not allowed to carry
updates.custom_requirements:
## What this test is about
The carrier only lets this store sell accessories that are on its approved list. The store's own catalog is bigger than that list - it still holds old items, store-made entries and products from other suppliers - and they all still show up when the rep browses. If Accessory Sale let any of them onto the invoice, the store would sell something it is not allowed to carry. So when the rep tries to add an accessory that is not on the approved list, the sale refuses it with a message naming the item, and the invoice stays as it was. This test walks a rep picking a not-approved accessory from the list and trying to add it.

## Related tickets
RTPL-3061, RTPL-3067, RTPL-3070 (approved accessory list for carrier-exclusive stores)

## Preconditions
- The rep is signed in at store EZLOGIC.
- The till has no customer tablet paired to it.
- The invoice is empty at the start.

## Test data
- **Accessory that is not on the approved list:** Item number SCREEN REPLACEMENT, $50.00, in stock  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-14, Browse accessories search: one row SCREEN REPLACEMENT, SRP $50.00; adding it produced the refusal message below)_
- **Expected refusal message:** Unapproved sku - SKU 'SCREEN REPLACEMENT' is not approved and cannot be added. Only approved accessories are allowed.  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-14, captured verbatim from the message that appeared after clicking Add accessories)_

## Screens (design reference)
- **Not-approved accessory refused** — screenshot: `screens/live-2026-10-14-05-unapproved-refused.png` (attach from the run folder)

## Automation Notes
- The message appears briefly at the top right of the screen and clears itself, so capture it at the moment Add accessories is clicked rather than looking for it later. Match the title and the explanation; the extra Code, Correlation ID and Timestamp lines under it change every run.
- The QTY figure changes whenever anyone sells or receives this item on the test environment, so check only that it is above zero - never assert an exact count.
- Check the invoice as well as the message - a refusal that still adds the line would be the more serious defect of the two.
- The panel shows the line Item Not Found under its heading for this item, because the catalog holds no description for it. Do not assert on that line; it is not the refusal.
- Clean up afterwards by cancelling the sale (Cart options, Cancel cart) if a cart is left open, so the next run starts with an empty invoice.
- If SCREEN REPLACEMENT is added without a refusal when you run this - it has been put on the approved list - contact the manual QA team to get another not-approved item number for this store rather than hunting for data alone.

steps.action: Login into the app
steps.expected: The dashboard opens and the header shows STORE ID EZLOGIC, DEALER CODE 30247306 and STATION showing the station the rep signed in on.

steps.action: On the dashboard, click the Accessory Sale tile
steps.expected: The Accessory Sale screen opens with the heading ACCESSORY SALE and an empty invoice reading Inventory $0.00 and Total due $0.00.

steps.action: Click Browse accessories, type SCREEN REPLACEMENT into the search box, then click that row
steps.expected: The list narrows to one row: SCREEN REPLACEMENT, a QTY above zero (stock on hand), SRP $50.00. Clicking it opens a panel headed Item detail SCREEN REPLACEMENT showing Price $50.00, Tax $5.00, Discount ($0.00) and Final price $55.00, with the buttons Add accessories and Close. Nothing on the panel warns that the item cannot be sold.

steps.action: Click Add accessories
steps.expected: The item is refused. A message appears reading Unapproved sku, with the explanation SKU 'SCREEN REPLACEMENT' is not approved and cannot be added. Only approved accessories are allowed. The message names the item the rep just tried to add.

steps.action: Read the invoice panel
steps.expected: The invoice is still empty - it reads Inventory $0.00 and Total due $0.00, and no line was added. The rep cannot carry a not-approved accessory into the sale.

steps.action: Stop here - do NOT click Continue and do not take any payment
steps.expected: The sale is left on the Add accessories screen with nothing on the invoice.
